usage: wsp projects
  your projects, each on its computer: where its code comes from, where its
  folder sits, the branch a machine of it starts on and how many threads it has

  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp projects remove <project> [--yes] [--force]
  takes a project out of this wsp; its folder is left where it is, on this
  computer or on a computer you joined, a project with a machine standing on it
  is refused naming them, and one whose checkout on a computer of yours holds
  work no remote has is stopped naming it

  --yes      go ahead without being asked
  --force    remove it even where its checkout on a computer of yours holds work
             no remote has, which goes with it
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp projects set <project> [--agent <id>] [--model <slug>]
       [--effort <word>] [--access <word>] [--after-worktree <command>]
       [--tracker <owner/name>]... [--reset <field>]...
  what a new thread on one project starts on, over the agent's own defaults: its
  agent, model, effort and access; the shell line a new worktree of it runs
  once, after each ecosystem's own install, for what none of them knows; and the
  repos besides its own that gh on a sub-thread's machine may comment on, the
  whole list each time

  --agent             the agent a new thread on it runs (claude, codex,
                      opencode, cursor)
  --model             the model a new thread on it starts on, by the agent's own
                      slug
  --effort            the effort a new thread on it starts at, by the agent's
                      own word
  --access            how far a new thread on it may go without asking: ask,
                      auto-edit, full or plan
  --after-worktree    a shell line a new worktree of the project runs once at
                      its top, after each ecosystem's own install
  --tracker           a repo, owner/name, besides the project's own that gh on a
                      sub-thread's machine may comment on; repeats, and the ones
                      named are the whole list
  --reset             put a field back on the layer below: agent, model, effort
                      or access, take the after-worktree command away with
                      after-worktree, or empty the trackers with trackers;
                      repeats
  --json              print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line,
                      with everything else on stderr
  --state             the state file the host serves
  --host              run the line against a host on your account, by the name
                      wsp hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole
                      shell

usage: wsp projects seed <project> [--keep <path>]... [--cut <path>]... [--none]
       [--yes]
  what git ignores in a project's folder on this computer, and which of it goes
  to a sub-thread's machine: the menu with each path's size and why, the picks
  marked; --yes saves the picks, which every later sub-thread of the project
  takes

  --keep     one more path off the menu that goes to a sub-thread's machine;
             given once per path
  --cut      one path off the menu that stays on this computer; given once per
             path
  --none     send no git-ignored file to a sub-thread's machine
  --yes      save the picks; without it the menu is printed and nothing is saved
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp threads [<project>] [--tree] [--watch]
  who is working, where and on which computer: every thread as the sidebar lists
  it, with its project, the folder it works in, that folder's branch, the agent,
  the state and who opened it, and under each thread the agent's own subagents
  with their SUBAGENT id; --tree indents the threads an agent spawned under the
  one that spawned them, and --watch draws the same table again every second
  where it stands

  --tree     indent the threads an agent opened under the one that opened them
  --watch    draw the table again every second where it stands, until Ctrl-C; it
             needs a terminal to redraw on
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp threads wait <thread>... [--timeout <s>] [--tail]
  blocks until one of the threads leaves running and prints its finished line,
  with the reply whole under it; --tail prints the reply's last line alone,
  which is what a notify sends, and --timeout gives up after so many seconds and
  says so on stderr

  --timeout    how long to wait before answering that they are still running
  --tail       print the reply's last line alone, the line a notify sends,
               rather than the whole reply
  --json       print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
               everything else on stderr
  --state      the state file the host serves
  --host       run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
               hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

  your projects, each on its computer: where its code comes from, where its
  folder sits, the branch a machine of it starts on and how many threads it has

  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with

  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
